_comment: Routing and dependency gates for the native AI platform OS implementation plan.
This file declares INTENT: who is assigned what, and what blocks what.
It never declares STATE. State is derived from git by scripts/task_status.py,
because a hand-maintained status table is how this repository accumulated eight
claim-defects. If this file and git disagree, git is right.
glm-5.3-flash  volume implementation once a task is expanded to step form
minimax-m3     all UI/UX surfaces, built against contract fixtures
opus           correctness-critical: adversarial design, judgment, review gate
human          requires hardware, a credential, or a machine nobody has run
branch_convention_note: Advisory only. The tracker matches any branch containing task-{id} as a segment, so feat/task-0.1-reputation-workspace, impl/task-0.1 and fix/task-0.1-x all resolve to the same task. The plan is authoritative on the exact name.

0.4.note: Task 0.4 lints tier disclosure across report, status AND console. Only Task 4.3 carries that rendering into the console and desktop, so only 4.3 collides. Tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.4 and 4.5 touch different files and can run concurrently with Phase 0 once Phase 4 is expanded.

phase_spine._note_phases_7_14: From docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-phases-7-14-scope.md. Phase 11 depends on Phase 4 and on nothing else: it extends the console Phase 4 built, so it is parallel to Phases 7-10 but not to Phase 4. It is NOT empty like Phase 4's own spine -- Phase 4 is off-spine because it builds against fixtures instead of a backend, whereas Phase 11 builds on Phase 4's actual files. With an empty spine the board called all thirteen Phase 11 tasks READY while the consolidated branch they extend did not exist.
phase_spine._note_phase_4: Deliberately empty. Phase 4 sits after Phase 3 in the plan's dependency spine, but MiniMax builds against frozen contract fixtures rather than a running backend, which is what makes the two lanes parallel. Only Task 4.3 is gated, on Task 0.4, via the gates block.

routing_notes.1.1: Keystone. Evidence and notary into the report path; everything in Phases 1-2 is meaningless until it lands. Review hardest.
routing_notes.1.5: One delegation algebra. Merging two implementations of one contract is a correctness decision, not volume work.
routing_notes.2.1: The effect decomposition registry is the architectural keystone of the syscall model. A wrong decomposition silently under-governs an effect.
routing_notes.3.2: Needs a TPM or an OS keystore observed executing. macOS has never been installed or launched in this project.
routing_notes.5.3: Do not delegate to a fast model. The value is an adversary that genuinely tries; one that fails trivially yields a green result and a false guarantee.
routing_notes.5.4: The drills are mechanical; naming shared failure domains is judgment.
routing_notes.4.3: Blocked on 0.4. It carries 0.4's tier rendering into the console and desktop; starting early collides on the same files.
routing_notes.4.1: The console is vanilla JavaScript (console.js, 1,824 lines) and desktop is Electron with zero runtime dependencies. Not TypeScript, not React. Do not introduce a framework or a bundler.
routing_notes.11.0: All thirteen Phase 11 tasks share one branch, feat/phase-11-operator-estate, deliberately. Wave 1 ran four parallel branches over console.js and they conflicted seven ways; thirteen would be worse. The phase is sequential.
routing_notes.10.10: Routed human for the same reason as 3.2: it needs decisions about jurisdiction and legal exposure, not code. It still produces a document on a branch.
routing_notes.14.11: Routed human. The only task in Phases 7-14 that creates an obligation to a third party rather than a control over an agent, so the commitment is the owner's to choose.

minimax_phase_4.blocked_until: Phase 4 expanded to step form (it is still stubs, so the board shows zero Phase 4 tasks); then 0.4 landed, but only for Task 4.3
minimax_phase_4.build_against: contract fixtures, not a running backend
minimax_phase_4.note: Phase 4 sits after Phase 3 in the spine, but contracts-first decouples it: the UI is built against frozen fixtures so the lanes run parallel.
